notes: MEXT (Japanese Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology) Embassy Recommendation Research Student scholarship is a national government scheme with no attached host institution. Selected MEXT scholars are placed individually at Japanese universities/research institutions of their choosing, which are confirmed only after selection through MEXT. No supervising professor is tied to the scholarship itself, so no supervisor enrichment is applicable.

ANRF Ramanujan Fellowship is a scientist-specific, reverse-brain-drain individual fellowship run by the Anusandhan National Research Foundation. The official ANRF scheme page (https://www.anrfonline.in/ANRF/Ramanujan_fellowship) states: 'The Ramanujan Fellows could work in any of the scientific institutions and universities in the country' and 'Individual Scientists and Technologists should approach the Institutions of his/her choice for hosting them.' There is no fixed host institution or named supervising faculty attached to the scheme.

Government of Ireland Postgraduate Scholarship Programme is a central, researcher-initiated government scheme managed by Research Ireland across all eligible Irish HEIs; nominees propose their own projects at any eligible institution. The official programme page (https://www.researchireland.ie/funding/government-ireland-postgraduate) confirms the programme is closed and integrated into the new Empower scheme, under which applications are institutional rather than individual. No institution-specific supervisors are attached to the scheme.

Ireland Fellows Programme is an Irish Aid (Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade) bilateral government scholarship placing roughly 224 fellows per year from 48 countries on one-year taught Master's programmes at various Irish higher education institutions, coordinated through Irish embassies. It is a central government scheme with no single attached institution and no research supervisor component.

notes: Hardiman PhD Scholarships at University of Galway are university-wide structured-PhD awards. The official scholarship page (https://universityofgalway.ie/hardiman-scholarships) requires every applicant to 'nominate one supervisor' and directs them to the university's official Find-a-Supervisor portal (https://www.universityofgalway.ie/findasupervisor/ -> research.universityofgalway.ie), which lists 499 staff profiles flagged 'Accepting PhD Students'. The three professors above are verified members of that official supervisor pool, each with a universityofgalway.ie email published on the profile itself. Because the scholarship spans all four colleges and all disciplines, this is a representative set of verified potential supervisors, not an exhaustive list.

Verified on the official DCU page (https://www.dcu.ie/global/dcu-international-scholarships-non-eu-students-2027-28) that this is an automatic, merit-based tuition-fee reduction (EUR 1,850-6,100) for non-EU applicants to taught undergraduate and postgraduate programmes across DCU's faculties and business school. Applicants are considered automatically with no research proposal and no supervisor nomination, so no supervising professor or faculty member is attached to this scholarship.

The official programme page (https://www.researchireland.ie/funding/government-ireland-postdoctoral) confirms the programme is closed and integrated into the new Empower scheme with institutional-level applications.
